## The Python Package Ecosystem

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-height: 7.5
%%{init: {"flowchart": {"nodeSpacing": 60, "rankSpacing": 70}}}%%
flowchart TB
  PE["<b>PyEns</b><br/>parallel ensemble runs"]
  PS["<b>pySIPNET</b><br/>one SIPNET run:<br/>inputs, outputs, units"]
  PK["<b>pyEKI</b><br/>ensemble Kalman inversion"]
  SC["<b>sipnet_calibration</b><br/>sites, data, priors<br/>and calibration"]
  PE -. optional .-> PS
  PS --> SC
  PE --> SC
  PK --> SC
```

::: notes
The three companions are separate repositories, installed here from git and
pinned to exact commits in uv.lock. pySIPNET works on its own; it uses PyEns
only when asked to run an ensemble.
:::

## The Modeling Pipeline

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 15.5
%%| fig-height: 7.5
%%{init: {"flowchart": {"nodeSpacing": 150}}}%%
flowchart LR
  S[Sites] --> T[PFTs]
  S --> P[Parameter vector]
  S --> D[Drivers]
  S --> I[Initial conditions]
  T -. optional .-> P
  T -. optional .-> I
  P --> M[SIPNET]
  D --> M
  I --> M
  M --> H[Observation operator]
  H --> L[Likelihood]
  C[Constraints] --> L
```

::: notes
Order of the talk follows the arrows: inputs first, then the parameter vector,
then how model output meets the data.
:::

# Meteorological drivers

## The ERA5 driver ensemble

Dongchen's SIPNET drivers, on the SCC at `{python} config.DRIVERS_SOURCE`:
the ERA5 ensemble (10 members, 3-hourly, 0.5°, 2012–2024), converted to SIPNET
`.clim` files by PEcAn.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Known issues

1. **The time labels drift.** PEcAn's `met2cf.ERA5` spread each year's labels
   over the wrong interval, by up to 2 hours at year end (fixed upstream in
   PEcAn PR #3584). The values sit on a regular 3-hour grid (pySIPNET checks 
   will error on the met files with the drift).
2. **Instantaneous values read as means.** Temperature, humidity, wind and
   pressure are instantaneous at the label; SIPNET treats every driver as a
   mean over the step.
3. **Accumulations are shifted one step.** Radiation and precipitation cover
   the 3 hours ending at the label; SIPNET reads each row as the 3 hours
   starting there.
4. **Soil temperature** comes from a PEcAn `stats::convolve` step that weights
   future air temperatures.
:::

- Every site in one 0.5° ERA5 grid cell has identical drivers.
- The plots here use copies with only the hour column corrected, so only issue
  1 is addressed.

# Initial conditions

## The initial condition ensemble

Dongchen's PEcAn initial conditions, on the SCC at
`{python} config.INITIAL_CONDITIONS_SOURCE`: 100 members at each of the 8000
sites, one file per site and member, converted here into one product.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Known issues

1. **Units are unconfirmed** for every variable.
2. **Wood goes negative**: it is the biomass draw minus the leaf draw, drawn
   independently. Drop, floor, or replace?
3. **Leaf carbon** is LAI / SLA with no carbon fraction applied: kg of leaf
   labeled kg C.
4. **Soil moisture** is percent of saturation; SIPNET's initial value is a
   fraction of its bucket's water holding capacity.
5. ISCN soil carbon stocks have an **undocumented integration depth**.
6. Which **PEcAn version** ran the reanalysis? The wood conversion changed on
   2025-09-02.
:::

- Leaf carbon and soil moisture are absent at some sites.
- Values are kept as the source files give them, negative draws included.
  Turning them into SIPNET's initial parameters needs calibrated parameters
  (leaf area is leaf carbon times specific leaf area), so that happens for
  each proposed parameter vector, not in the product.

# Parameters

## From the sampler to SIPNET

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 15.5
%%| fig-height: 5.5
%%{init: {"flowchart": {"nodeSpacing": 70, "rankSpacing": 80}}}%%
flowchart LR
  U["<b>θ in ℝ<sup>D</sup></b><br/>unconstrained<br/>where EKI/MCMC operate"]
  N["<b>ϑ<sub>c</sub></b><br/>calibration parameter<br/>in natural space,<br/>where the prior is defined"]
  S["<b>SIPNET parameters</b><br/>aMax, baseFolRespFrac,<br/>leafAllocation, ..."]
  F["<b>fixed SIPNET parameters</b><br/>aMaxFrac, cFracLeaf, ..."]
  R["<b>SIPNET run</b>"]
  U -- "T<sub>c</sub>: bijector<br/>invertible" --> N
  N -- "M<sub>c</sub>: SIPNET map" --> S
  F -- "read by M<sub>c</sub>" --> S
  S --> R
```

- **T~c~** is chosen according to parameter constraints; e.g., exp for a positive paramter
- **M~c~** folds in fixed parameters, so it need not be invertible.
- I've set up the code so each calibration parameter is shared, has one copy per PFT (or other grouping), or one copy per site.

## Example: Photosynthesis parameterization

SIPNET uses its four photosynthesis parameters only through

$$
A = \frac{\texttt{aMax}\cdot\texttt{aMaxFrac}}{\texttt{cFracLeaf}},
\qquad
R = \frac{\texttt{aMax}\cdot\texttt{baseFolRespFrac}}{\texttt{cFracLeaf}},
$$

the gross photosynthetic capacity and the basal foliar respiration per unit
of leaf carbon.

- Any change to the four that keeps $A$ and $R$ fixed leaves every output
  unchanged
- We can calibrate two parameters, and fix $\texttt{aMaxFrac}$ and $\texttt{cFracLeaf}$.

## Photosynthesis: T and M

The calibration parameter is capacity and respiration share,
$\vartheta = (P, \rho)$ with $P = A + R$ and $\rho = R / (A + R)$.

$$
T:\ \theta \in \mathbb{R}^2 \ \mapsto\ (P, \rho) = \big(e^{\theta_1},\ \sigma(\theta_2)\big),
\qquad \sigma(x) = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-x}}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
M:\ (P, \rho) \ &\mapsto\ \big(\texttt{aMax},\ \texttt{baseFolRespFrac}\big) \\
&= \left(\frac{P\,\texttt{cFracLeaf}\,(1 - \rho)}{\texttt{aMaxFrac}},\ \frac{\rho\,\texttt{aMaxFrac}}{1 - \rho}\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

$M$ reads the fixed $\texttt{aMaxFrac}$ and $\texttt{cFracLeaf}$.

## Allocation: T and M

The calibration parameter is the carbon allocation to leaf, wood, fine root
and coarse root, a point on the simplex: $\vartheta = \pi = (\pi_1, \pi_2, \pi_3, \pi_4)$,
$\pi_i > 0$, $\sum_i \pi_i = 1$.

$$
T:\ \theta \in \mathbb{R}^3 \ \mapsto\ \pi, \qquad
\pi_i = \frac{e^{\theta_i}}{1 + \sum_{j=1}^{3} e^{\theta_j}}\ (i \le 3),
\qquad
\pi_4 = \frac{1}{1 + \sum_{j=1}^{3} e^{\theta_j}}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
M:\ \pi \ &\mapsto\ \big(\texttt{leafAllocation},\ \texttt{woodAllocation},\ \texttt{fineRootAllocation}\big) \\
&= (\pi_1, \pi_2, \pi_3)
\end{aligned}
$$

SIPNET recomputes coarse root as $1 - (\pi_1 + \pi_2 + \pi_3)$ and exits if it
is not positive; keeping $\pi_4$ in $\vartheta$ ensures we don't have to wait for 
SIPNET to run to catch this error.

# Other data issues

## Other data issues

**NEE**

- Potential timezone issue for NEE: timestamps to UTC through a time zone with 
daylight saving: values sit 3 to 5 hours from their labels

**Soil texture** (the input for SIPNET's water holding capacity, `soilWHC`; not
used yet)

- 307 of the 8000 sites have no files.
- PEcAn sets `soilWHC` to porosity integrated over 2 m: 73 to 101 cm, against
  12 cm in SIPNET's template and above the template's own upper bound of 36 cm.
- Issues I have noted in Slack regarding soil physics workflow
